quote: EnemyElite.as:102 'var baseSlashLength:int = 120 + Math.floor(maxincrement * val / (20 + val));' with :101 'var maxincrement:int = 90;' and :100 'var val:int = xml.speed;' · web §1t99s0§.as:194 'this.§1t4420s0§ = param10;'
text: hunter-s27b/heavy-reach-has-a-hard-100px-floor records its one remaining unknown as 'the base value 1t4420s0 ... which is set elsewhere and which I did not resolve'. It resolves. Web: 1t99s0.as:105 initialises 1t4420s0 to 10, :194 assigns it from the tenth initPlayer parameter, and :223 halves it ('*= 0.5') in one branch. The android twin is positionally identical - MCSPlayer.as:107 'internal var baseSlashLength:int = 10;', :182 declares initPlayer with baseSlashLength as its tenth parameter, :193 assigns it, :222 halves it - which names 1t4420s0 = baseSlashLength. The value fed in, for NPCs, is computed by the caller: EnemyElite.as:102 baseSlashLength = 120 + floor(90 * speed / (20 + speed)), i.e. a saturating curve from 120 px at speed 0 toward 210 px, 165 px at speed 20. So reach = baseSlashLength x per-stance multiplier, and at the low end the 100 px heavy floor genuinely bites: base 120 at mastery 0 gives 60, clamped up to 100. CAVEAT, stated plainly: the formula line is android v0.682, so under S0-3/C2 it is v0.682 until a web caller is read; what IS web-attested is that the base is an injected per-fighter slash length with a halving branch, not a global constant. lane_impact: Gauntlet tooling: reduces false QUOTE_UNVERIFIED flags across every remaining packet. NOT applied - this lane is forbidden to modify files outside its journal.
text: Both QUOTE_UNVERIFIED claims in this packet had byte-exact quotes, and they are the only two claims in the packet that delimited their quotes with BACKTICKS instead of straight or curly quotes. citeLint's QUOTED_SPAN_RE recognises only double quotes, curly quotes and single quotes - a backticked span never becomes a candidate, so the check falls back to 6-word shingles and long tokens, which in this corpus straddle the ' · ' separators and the 'file.as:NNNN' prefixes and land nowhere. I re-ran the five affected lines as exact string comparisons after strip(): §1t99s0§.as:249, :3050, :3060, :3272 and :3274 all match their quoted text character for character. This is worth fixing because the packet's instruction makes QUOTE_UNVERIFIED the top-priority refute target, so a purely cosmetic delimiter choice is currently steering critics toward refuting sound claims - the exact over-refutation failure mode §0 warns about. Adding a backtick alternative to QUOTED_SPAN_RE is a one-token fix.
